```{r}
#| include: false
source("assets/setup.R")
source("assets/quiz.R")
cc <- ncd |> drop_na(sbp, htn, salt_g, age, bmi, waist, sex, residence, education, tobacco, alcohol, phys_act)
f_rhs <- "salt_g + age + bmi + sex + residence + education + tobacco + alcohol + phys_act"
m_lin <- lm(reformulate(f_rhs, "sbp"), data = cc)
m_log <- glm(reformulate(f_rhs, "htn"), data = cc, family = binomial)
sl <- tidy(m_lin, conf.int = TRUE) |> filter(term == "salt_g")
so <- tidy(m_log, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |> filter(term == "salt_g")
r2s <- summary(m_lin)
roc_obj <- roc(cc$htn, fitted(m_log), quiet = TRUE)
f1 <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
```

# Topic 9 — Reading the output {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Linear regression: what each number means

```{r}
#| echo: false
tibble(
  Output = c("β (salt_g)", "Std. error", "95% CI", "p-value", "R² / adjusted R²", "Residual SE"),
  Value  = c(f1(sl$estimate, 2), f1(sl$std.error, 2), paste0(f1(sl$conf.low), " to ", f1(sl$conf.high)),
             "< 0.001", paste0(f1(r2s$r.squared, 2), " / ", f1(r2s$adj.r.squared, 2)), paste0(f1(sigma(m_lin)), " mmHg")),
  `How to say it` = c(
    "Each extra 1 g/day of salt ↔ this many mmHg higher mean SBP, other variables held constant",
    "Precision of β: smaller = more precise",
    "Plausible range for the true β — report it with every estimate",
    "Chance of a β this far from 0 if the true β were 0 — not the size of the effect",
    "Share of SBP variability the model accounts for — descriptive only",
    "The typical size of a prediction miss, in mmHg")
) |> knitr::kable()
```

## Logistic regression: what each number means

```{r}
#| echo: false
tibble(
  Output = c("OR (salt_g)", "95% CI", "p-value", "Null → residual deviance", "AIC", "Pseudo-R² (McFadden / Tjur)", "AUC"),
  Value  = c(f1(so$estimate, 2), paste0(f1(so$conf.low, 2), " to ", f1(so$conf.high, 2)), "< 0.001",
             paste0(f1(m_log$null.deviance, 0), " → ", f1(deviance(m_log), 0)), f1(AIC(m_log), 0),
             paste0(f1(r2_mcfadden(m_log)$R2[[1]], 2), " / ", f1(r2_tjur(m_log)[[1]], 2)), f1(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 2)),
  `How to say it` = c(
    "Each extra 1 g/day multiplies the ODDS of hypertension by this factor, adjusted",
    "Plausible range for the OR; if it contains 1, no clear association",
    "As for linear regression",
    "How much the covariates improve the likelihood-based fit",
    "Use to compare models fitted to the same rows (lower = better)",
    "Descriptive; not 'variance explained'; do not compare with linear R²",
    "Discrimination: 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect")
) |> knitr::kable()
```

## A publication-ready combined table

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
labs <- list(salt_g ~ "Salt intake (per 1 g/day)", age ~ "Age (per year)", bmi ~ "BMI (per kg/m²)",
             sex ~ "Sex", residence ~ "Residence", education ~ "Education", tobacco ~ "Tobacco use",
             alcohol ~ "Alcohol use", phys_act ~ "Physical activity")
t_lin <- tbl_regression(m_lin, label = labs) |> bold_labels()
t_log <- tbl_regression(m_log, exponentiate = TRUE, label = labs) |> bold_labels()
tbl_merge(list(t_lin, t_log), tab_spanner = c("**Systolic BP (β, mmHg)**", "**Hypertension (OR)**")) |>
  modify_header(estimate_1 ~ "**β**", estimate_2 ~ "**OR**")
```

# Topic 10 — Writing it up {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Results sentence — linear regression

::: {.key}
"After adjusting for age, BMI, sex, residence, education, tobacco, alcohol and physical activity, **each 1 g/day higher salt intake was associated with a `r f1(sl$estimate)` mmHg higher systolic blood pressure (95% CI `r f1(sl$conf.low)` to `r f1(sl$conf.high)`; p < 0.001)** (n = `r nrow(cc)`; adjusted R² = `r f1(r2s$adj.r.squared, 2)`)."
:::

::: {.incremental}
- ✔ **Direction + size + units** · ✔ **CI** · ✔ **adjustment set** · ✔ **n** · ✔ "associated with"
- Give the **crude** estimate too (`r f1(coef(lm(sbp ~ salt_g, cc))[[2]])` mmHg) so readers see the effect of adjustment
:::

## Results sentence — logistic regression

::: {.key}
"Hypertension was present in `r f1(100 * mean(cc$htn), 0)`% of participants. After adjustment, **each 1 g/day higher salt intake was associated with `r f1(100 * (so$estimate - 1), 0)`% higher odds of hypertension (adjusted OR `r f1(so$estimate, 2)`; 95% CI `r f1(so$conf.low, 2)` to `r f1(so$conf.high, 2)`)**. The model showed good discrimination (AUC `r f1(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 2)`)."
:::

::: {.incremental}
- ✔ **Say "odds"** (not risk) · ✔ **unit of x** · ✔ **reference categories** for categorical ORs
- With a **common outcome**, add the **prevalence ratio** if you want to say "times as likely"
:::

## Tables and figures: what a reader needs

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.good}
**Include**

- **Units** in row labels (per g/day, per 5 kg/m²)
- **Reference category** for every categorical variable
- **n** analysed (note missing data handling)
- **95% CI** (not only p)
- **Footnote**: adjustment set, abbreviations, model type
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.bad}
**Avoid**

- "p = 0.000" (write p < 0.001)
- Stars-only tables
- Reporting β **without** the outcome units
- Hiding the crude estimates
:::
:::
:::

## The Methods paragraph

::: {.incremental}
1. **Model and why** — "multiple linear regression for SBP; logistic regression for hypertension (SBP ≥ 140 or DBP ≥ 90)"
2. **Covariates and rationale** — "chosen a priori from a causal diagram/literature, not by automated selection"
3. **Assumption checks** — linearity, independence (clustering by village), residual normality, equal variance, collinearity (VIF); and how violations were handled
4. **Missing data** — "complete-case analysis; n = …"
5. **Model assessment** (logistic) — likelihood ratio tests, AIC, calibration, AUC
6. **Software** — R version and packages (below)
:::

## Software line: let R tell you

```{r}
R.version.string
sapply(c("tidyverse", "gtsummary", "broom", "performance", "pROC", "car", "lmtest"),
       \(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)))
```

::: {.fragment}
"Analyses were done in R `r paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")` using the tidyverse, gtsummary, performance, car, lmtest and pROC packages." Follow **STROBE** for observational studies.
:::

# Common pitfalls {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Pitfall 1 — Stepwise selection presented as *the* analysis

::: {.bad}
"Variables were selected by backward stepwise regression (AIC)." → biased β, narrow CIs, unstable model, ignores confounding logic.
:::

::: {.good}
**Instead:** pre-specify covariates from a **DAG or the literature**; report the same model whatever the p-values. If you use `step()`, label it **exploratory** (Session 3 demos).
:::

## Pitfall 2 — "p < 0.2 into the model"

```{r}
vars <- c("salt_g", "age", "bmi", "sex", "residence", "education", "tobacco", "alcohol", "phys_act")
p_uni <- map_dbl(vars, \(v) anova(glm(reformulate(v, "htn"), binomial, cc), test = "LRT")$`Pr(>Chi)`[2])
or_adj <- tidy(m_log, exponentiate = TRUE) |> filter(term %in% c("phys_actmoderate", "phys_acthigh", "residenceRural"))
tibble(variable = vars, `univariable p` = signif(p_uni, 2)) |> filter(variable %in% c("phys_act", "residence", "salt_g"))
or_adj |> select(term, `adjusted OR` = estimate, p.value) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 2)))
```

::: {.fragment}
::: {.bad}
Physical activity has **univariable p ≈ 1** — a "p < 0.2" screen would **drop it** — yet adjusted for age, BMI and sex, **high activity has OR ≈ 0.57**. Confounding hides it from the crude test.
:::
:::

## Pitfalls 3–6: say it properly {.smaller}

| Pitfall | ✘ Don't | ✔ Do |
|---|---|---|
| **3. β without units or reference** | "Salt β = 1.8; sex β = 3.8" | "1.8 mmHg higher SBP per 1 g/day; men 3.8 mmHg higher than women (reference)" |
| **4. OR read as risk** | "50+ y are 5.1 times as likely to be hypertensive" (outcome 32%) | "…had 5.1 times the odds (PR 3.1)" |
| **5. Pseudo-R² as R²** | "The model explains 29% of the variance in hypertension" | "Tjur's R² was 0.29 (a descriptive pseudo-R²)" |
| **6. Statistical = clinical** | "Highly significant (p < 0.001), therefore important" | "A 1.8 mmHg difference per g/day (95% CI 1.2–2.4): a 5 g reduction ≈ 9 mmHg lower mean SBP" |

## Pitfall 7 — Overfitting: too few events per variable

```{r}
events <- sum(cc$htn); params <- length(coef(m_log)) - 1
c(events = events, parameters = params, events_per_variable = round(events / params, 1))
```

::: {.incremental}
- Rule of thumb: **≥ 10 events per variable** (events = the *smaller* outcome group); our model has `r round(events/params, 1)` — acceptable
- Too many predictors → the model memorises noise: **great on this sample, poor on the next**
:::

## Overfitting in action: 60 pure-noise predictors

```{r}
set.seed(3)
noise <- as_tibble(matrix(rnorm(nrow(cc) * 60), ncol = 60)); d_o <- bind_cols(htn = cc$htn, noise)
train <- sample(nrow(d_o), 300)
g_o <- glm(htn ~ ., binomial, d_o[train, ])
auc_in  <- auc(roc(d_o$htn[train],  fitted(g_o), quiet = TRUE))
auc_out <- auc(roc(d_o$htn[-train], predict(g_o, d_o[-train, ], type = "response"), quiet = TRUE))
round(c(AUC_on_training_data = as.numeric(auc_in), AUC_on_new_data = as.numeric(auc_out)), 2)
```

::: {.fragment}
Pure noise can look **"good"** on the data that built it (AUC well above 0.5) and falls back toward **0.5** on new data — the signature of overfitting.
:::

## Pitfall 8 — Ignoring assumptions and clustering

```{r}
se_naive   <- summary(m_lin)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"]
se_cluster <- sqrt(diag(sandwich::vcovCL(m_lin, cluster = cc$village)))
tibble(term = names(se_naive), naive_SE = round(se_naive, 2), village_robust_SE = round(se_cluster, 2),
       ratio = round(se_cluster / se_naive, 2)) |> filter(term %in% c("salt_g", "age", "residenceRural"))
```

::: {.incremental}
- For **village-level** predictors (residence) the true SE is noticeably **larger** than the naive SE — naive CIs are too narrow
- Individual-level predictors (salt) are less affected here, but you should still **state** the design and check assumptions
- Remedies: mixed models, GEE, cluster-robust SE, survey methods (next slides)
:::

## Pitfall 9 — Calling associations causal

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.bad}
- "Salt **causes** hypertension (β = 1.8)"
- "Tobacco **increases** SBP by 3 mmHg"
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.good}
- "Higher salt intake was **associated with** higher SBP"
- "Tobacco users **had** 3 mmHg higher mean SBP"
:::
:::
:::

::: {.incremental}
- A **cross-sectional** survey cannot establish **temporal order**
- Adjustment handles **measured** confounders only; the **DAG** states your assumptions
- Causal claims need design (RCT, strong quasi-experiment) and **explicit causal reasoning**
:::

## Before you submit

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
1. Outcome type matches the model
2. Covariates pre-specified, with rationale
3. Crude **and** adjusted estimates
4. Units and reference categories
5. CIs, not just p
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
6. Assumptions checked and reported
7. Events per variable adequate
8. Clustering / design acknowledged
9. OR vs PR considered for common outcomes
10. Language: **association**, not causation
:::
:::

# Beyond this workshop {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Other outcome types {.smaller}

| Model | Packages | When you'd use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Poisson / negative binomial** | `MASS::glm.nb` (and `glm(family = poisson)`) | **Counts** (dengue cases per ward, clinic visits); use NB when variance > mean; add an offset for person-time |
| **Ordinal logistic** | `MASS::polr`, `ordinal` | **Ordered categories** (BP stage, CKD stage, Likert satisfaction) |
| **Multinomial logistic** | `nnet::multinom` | **Unordered categories** (facility chosen, contraceptive method) |
| **Cox proportional hazards** | `survival` | **Time-to-event** with censoring (time to TB cure, relapse, death) |

## Data structure and design {.smaller}

| Model | Packages | When you'd use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Mixed (multilevel) models** | `lme4` | **Clustered or repeated** data (villages, PHCs, repeated visits); subject-specific effects |
| **GEE** | `geepack` | Same clustering when you want **population-average** effects with robust SEs |
| **Complex survey data** | `survey`, `srvyr` | **NFHS / NSSO-type** surveys with strata, PSUs and sampling weights |

::: {.warn}
Our villages are exactly why Session 4's independence assumption matters: a **mixed model** or **GEE** is the natural next step.
:::

## Flexible models and helpful tools {.smaller}

| Model or tool | Packages | When you'd use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Splines and GAMs** | `splines`, `mgcv` | **Non-linear** effects (age curve) without forcing a straight line or a polynomial |
| **Penalised regression** | `glmnet` | **Many or correlated predictors**, few events; lasso/ridge for prediction models |
| **Bayesian regression** | `brms` | **Small samples**, prior information, complex hierarchical models, full uncertainty |
| **Regression modelling strategy** | `rms` | Harrell's toolkit: validation (bootstrap), nomograms, restricted cubic splines |
| **Reporting and plots** | `modelsummary`, `sjPlot`, `broom`, `easystats` | Tidy extraction, publication tables, coefficient and effect plots, diagnostics |

## Take-home messages of the day

::: {.incremental}
1. **Outcome type → model**; regression gives effects **in units**, with CIs
2. **Confounding** is why we adjust: crude ≠ adjusted
3. Choose covariates from **theory**, not from stepwise or p-values
4. **Check assumptions** — and say what you did about violations
5. Logistic: **exp(β) = OR**; assess with **likelihood**, **calibration** and **discrimination**; mind **OR vs PR**
6. **Report** like a scientist: units, references, CIs, limitations — and **association ≠ causation**
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/6) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s6q1", "Which sentence reports a linear regression result correctly?",
         c("Salt β = 1.8 (p < 0.001)",
           "Salt had a significant effect on SBP",
           "Each 1 g/day higher salt intake was associated with 1.8 mmHg higher SBP (95% CI 1.2 to 2.4), adjusted for age, BMI and other covariates",
           "Salt explains 1.8% of blood pressure"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Report direction, size WITH units, CI, adjustment set and use 'associated with'. A bare β or p-value is not enough.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/6) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s6q2", "Why is 'keep variables with univariable p < 0.2' a poor strategy?",
         c("It keeps too few variables", "A variable can look unrelated alone yet matter after adjustment (confounding), and screening ignores causal reasoning",
           "It always overfits", "p-values cannot be computed for single variables"), answer = 2,
         explain = "In our data physical activity had univariable p ≈ 1 but an adjusted OR of about 0.57. Choose covariates from theory (DAG/literature), not crude p-values.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/6) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s6q3", "A cross-sectional survey finds higher salt intake is associated with higher SBP. Which conclusion is appropriate?",
         c("Salt intake causes hypertension", "Reducing salt will lower SBP by exactly the coefficient in everyone",
           "Higher salt intake was associated with higher SBP; causation cannot be established from this design alone",
           "There is no association because R² is low"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Cross-sectional data show association, not temporal order. Adjustment only handles measured confounders. Use association language and discuss limitations.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/6) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s6q4", "Using the rule of thumb of at least 10 events per variable, about how many predictors can a logistic model with 60 events support?",
         c("3", "6", "12", "60"), answer = 2,
         explain = "60 events ÷ 10 events per variable ≈ 6 predictors (counting every dummy variable). More than that risks overfitting.")
```
